records.description: A BGP route hijack affecting Amazon Route 53 DNS infrastructure redirected some DNS resolution for myetherwallet.com to a malicious server. Users who proceeded through the invalid TLS certificate warning could submit wallet credentials to the phishing site, and the attacker used stolen information to transfer Ethereum.
records.notes: The incident is scoped to the public web/DNS path rather than a compromise of MEW application code or wallet servers. MEW stated that its Chrome extension and locally run/offline copies were not affected. Cloudflare's network analysis attributes the hijacked DNS routes to Amazon Route 53; WLR does not preserve the early Google-DNS attribution from the initial MEW statement. No exact loss amount is canonicalized in this candidate.
records.title: BGP and DNS hijack redirected MyEtherWallet web users to a phishing site

records.description: MyEtherWallet's first-party ten-year retrospective states that its full-fledged MEW wallet app was released in March 2020 after the earlier MEWconnect signer-app lineage.
records.notes: Month precision only. The reviewed first-party retrospective establishes March 2020 but not one defensible exact release day. Canonical product wlr_prod_000076 is corrected from unresolved launch_date to 2020-03 with month precision. This is the full-fledged MEW wallet app, not the earlier MEWconnect signer app.
records.title: Full-fledged MEW wallet mobile app released

records.notes: First-party history dates the original Ether Wallet Generator to August 11, 2015 and preserves continuity into MyEtherWallet.
records.title: 10 Years of MyEtherWallet: Evolving with Ethereum

records.notes: First-party current overview identifies MEW Mobile for iOS and Android and states that MEW remains non-custodial, open-source and client-side.
records.title: MyEtherWallet: An Introduction

records.notes: MEW's official incident statement says its domain's public DNS path was hijacked and users were redirected to a phishing site. Follow-up statements from the MEW team say the Chrome extension and locally run copies were not affected.
records.title: Official statement regarding DNS spoofing of MyEtherWallet domain

records.notes: Cloudflare's first-hand BGP and DNS-resolver analysis attributes the hijacked prefixes to Amazon Route 53 DNS, observes malicious responses specifically for myetherwallet.com, and reports that stolen login information was used to transfer Ethereum.
records.title: BGP leaks and cryptocurrencies
